assumptions: Reference model: exact profile/project/shot/version identity is represented by one abstract identity; concurrent and multi-profile product execution is not exhaustively modeled.
Project and Library index acknowledgements are separate boundaries, not one transaction.
Every modeled responsive boundary settles or rejects; interruption is explicitly modeled as UNKNOWN. This is an assumption to verify, not an implementation guarantee.
Finite abstract response steps represent the approved finite response policy, not a selected numeric product timeout.
Reconciliation assumes dependencies restored, independent exact readback and original operation identity; implementation correspondence remains partial.
No cross-device or device-loss guarantee; actual media and authenticated persistent storage must remain present.

transitions.action: finite abstract response policy reveals interruption
resume original operation under restored dependencies
independent exact recovery confirms both boundaries
revalidate exact saved identity before approval
interrupted approval retains work without Locked
new edit cannot borrow previous acknowledgement

correspondenceRows.mechanism: Captured project bytes, queued HTTP writes, index synchronization, authority epoch and revision guard; each acknowledgement is separate.
gaps: Source mapping is partial; interrupted write/retry/operation identity and exact downstream acknowledgement require independent observation.

gaps.detail: privateMutation has no request deadline; a fetch that never resolves can keep pendingWrite and flushProfilePrivateWrites pending indefinitely. Confirm applicable product path and fix through a fresh issue at #2943.
Project commit may precede index synchronization failure. Exact interrupted durable state and original-operation retry/deduplication consistency are not proved by treating HTTP writes as atomic.
Existing two-process encrypted-storage fixture is not the normal Human Windows launcher and rendered Storyboard/Previs observation.

Client revision/profile guards and captured-byte queueing have bounded references; distributed server concurrency, late revision acknowledgement and full exact media/approval correspondence require scoped evidence.
